title: ONE INSET FOR THE RAID HUD PANELS, ONE CARD FOR THE CLOCK AND THE EXTRACT LINE
why: The Codex critic on the raid HUD (o-120d, 3 3 3 2, stuck over two rounds): the roster started 10 px from the left edge, the vitals 24, the right column 17 and the ammo card 8 from the right, so every corner had its own margin; the clock, its sky icon, the extract chip and the arrow floated as four pieces over a busy backdrop; the roster ran eight rows at one weight. Now every corner panel stands the same distance from its screen edge (the right column inset, 16.8 px at 1080p): the pillager board, the feed with the controls list and the medal spot, the status icons, the vitals bars, the teammate rows and the ammo card. Without a score card the clock, its sky icon, the extract line and its arrow stand on one centred card; with a score card (career, demo) the clock and score keep their own windows by his order and the extract line and its arrow share one card as wide as the score card. The teammate rows use the shared panel. YOU is the bright row of the pillager board and the rivals sit one step back.
now: Corner panels sit on one margin; the clock and the extract line share one card; the pillager board reads YOU first.
